text.p: A man convicted of murdering a Houston bait shop owner during a botched 1984 robbery was executed in Texas on Tuesday hours after an accomplice confessed to firing the fatal shot, a prison spokesman said.

Anthony Ray Westley, 36, died in the death house of the state prison here after the U.S. Supreme Court and a federal appeals court rejected eleventh-hour appeals based on the confession and Texas Governor George Bush refused to intercede.

"I didn't shoot your husband. I really didn't. I want you to believe I didn't kill him," Westley said to members of the victim's family who witnessed the execution, prison spokesman David Nunnelee said.
"I love you all," he said, turning to members of his family wailing and pounding on a glass partition separating them from the death chamber where he lay strapped to a gurney, Nunnelee said.

Westley was found guilty and sentenced to die for the murder of Chester Frank Hall, 39, who was shot in the back during an April 1984 robbery at Eileen's Bait and Tackle Shop, a small store he owned with his wife.

Westley and two accomplices entered the store as Hall was leaving for lunch and ordered a clerk to the floor at gunpoint. Seeing the robbery in progress, Hall ran back into the store with a gun drawn, prosecutors said.

Hall exchanged gunfire with the men but was cornered by Westley and accomplice John Dale Henry in a back room, where he was shot at close range, prosecutors said. A second accomplice, Tyrone Dunbar, also was killed in the shootout.

Hours before today's execution, Westley's attorneys said they obtained a copy of a taped telephone conversation in which Henry claimed responsibilty for shooting Hall as the two exchanged shots in the back of the store.
"After he shot me, I shot him," Henry said in a secretly taped conversation early on Tuesday morning with Marie Walker, Dunbar's stepdaughter, and other members of his family.
Dunbar's family had suspected Dunbar may have been shot during the robbery by Henry. Dunbar's wife, Martha Walker-Dunbar, said she was pregnant at the time with Henry's daughter.

"I do not want to see an innocent man executed for a murder he did not commit, while the guilty man walks free -- even if that man is the father of one of my children," Walker-Dunbar said in a sworn statement to the appeals court.
Henry was convicted and sentenced to 15 years in prison for aggravated robbery. He recently was paroled and contacted Walker-Dunbar hoping to see his daughter, the attorneys said.

Westley was the tenth person executed in Texas this year and the 117th since the death penalty was reinstated in the state in 1982. Texas leads the nation in the number of executions since the U.S. Supreme Court restored capital punishment in 1976.
